summary.tldr: Raises Criminal Code penalties for mischief involving buildings, objects or cemeteries used for religious worship.
what_it_does: Adds a new Criminal Code rule for mischief done to buildings or parts of buildings mainly used for religious worship, related worship objects, and cemeteries.
Requires at least $1,000 paid to the property owner for a first offence.
Requires at least $1,000 and 14 days in jail for a second offence, and at least $1,000 and 30 days in jail for later offences.
Allows up to 10 years in prison if the offence is prosecuted by indictment, or up to two years less a day if it is dealt with by summary conviction.
summary.background: The bill amends section 430 of the Criminal Code. Its drafters say it would increase the punishment for mischief relating to religious property.
